newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures choppy after factory data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures choppy after factory data.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures continued to bobble around unchanged levels after the release of weaker than expected U.S. factory orders for May.
The data, released at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT, helped Treasury bond futures firm slightly, supporting stock futures in turn, but the gains were muted, traders said.
"With the Fed coming in, bounces of any size are going to be limited," said one S&P floor trader for a U.S. brokerage.
May factory orders were reported down 0.7 percent, below analysts' expectations for a 0.2 percent decline. In April, orders rose a revised 1.4 percent.

The Federal Open Market Committee concludes its two-day meeting this afternoon, and while most market participants continue to believe monetary policy will be kept steady, the focus has turned to what the market might do immediately after the outcome is known, floor traders said.
Trading activity in stock index futures, which has been thin and choppy all week, has picked up this morning as investors position themselves for the conclusion of the meeting, they said.
Some S&P traders look for a late-day bounce assuming the Fed leaves interest rates unchanged.
"With no policy change we should get a pretty decent rally out of it," one S&P floor trader predicted.
He looked for the September contract to climb to 909.00 or 910.00 this afternoon but did not expect the contract high of 912.40 to be challenged.
He also said he expected a profit-taking dip to precede the FOMC announcement.
But other traders were less certain that a rally would follow a steady rate decision, fearing such positive news was already built into prices during Tuesday's runup.
Floor traders placed initial resistance for September S&Ps at 905.00, with support seen first at 899.00 to 898.00, then around 896.50.
Market attention is already turning to Thursday's U.S. employment data, traders said. The data release was moved back a day due to the July 4 holiday.
Nonfarm payrolls are seen rising 222,000, compared with a gain of 138,000 in May, and the unemployment rate is seen unchanged at 4.8 percent.
Financial futures markets are closed Friday for the July 4 holiday and will trade a shortened session on Thursday.

Sept S&Ps were up 1.95 at 903.20, NYSE New Composites up 1.40 at 472.25, Nikkeis up 15 at 20,290, Midcap 400s up 0.50 at 293.25, Nasdaq 100s up 4.05 at 971.50 and Russell 2000s up 1.10 at 399.00. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
